title: Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Technician (MGySgt to Sgt) PMOS, DC I&L
raw_text:
3. MOS 2336, Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Technician (MGySgt to Sgt)
PMOS, DC I&L

    a. Summary. Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) Technicians perform
various duties may include locating, accessing, identifying, rendering safe,
neutralizing, and disposing of hazards from foreign and domestic, chemical
biological radiological nuclear and high-yield explosive (CBRNE), unexploded
explosive ordnance (UXO), improvised explosive device (IED), and weapons of
mass destruction (WMD) that present a threat to operations, installations,
personal, or material.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess a GT score of 110 or higher.

            (2) Must be a U.S. citizen (cannot be a dual citizen).

        (3) Must be screened per NAVMC Form 11361, Explosive Ordnance
Disposal (EOD) Lateral Move Screening Checklist.

        (4) Prior to entry into EOD School, Marines must have sufficient
obligated service to allow 36 months remaining upon graduation.

        (5) Must meet the medical requirements listed in article 15-107 of
reference (aj) for explosive handling and/or explosive driver.

        (6) Must have a first class physical fitness test (PFT) and combat
fitness test (CFT) (accomplished during the EOD screening process).

        (7) Must have normal color vision and no claustrophobic tendencies
(bomb suit agility test will be administered during the EOD screening).

        (8) Be a volunteer in the grade of sergeant or corporal in any MOS.
Sergeants requesting a lateral move to EOD must not be selected for staff
sergeant in their current MOS.

        (9) Must undergo computerized neurocognitive assessment testing at
NAVSCOLEOD using the automated neuropsychological assessment metrics (ANAM)
test prior to beginning training.

        (10) Security requirement: must be eligible for a top-secret
security clearance based on a completed single scope background investigation
(SSBI)/tier 5 (T-5) investigation. Applications for the SSBI/T-5 must be
submitted prior to attendance of EOD School, Eglin AFB Florida.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the DOD Joint Explosive Ordnance Disposal Basic (Common
Core) Course (N56GPX1) at Eglin AFB, FL.

            (2) Requirements for continued qualification and progression training
are:

            (a) All EOD Technicians will be annually screened for continued
service in the EOD MOS using NAVMC Form 11362. Based on the comprehensive
standards covered under NAVMC 11362, EOD technicians will not be screened
using NAVMC Form 11386.




                                        3-152                         Enclosure (1)
 3121                                                                    NAVMC 1200.1L



            (b) The following core competencies must be trained to sustained
by all EOD technicians:

                    1.     Render safe of explosive ordnance (EO)

                    2.     WMD operations.

                    3.     IED defeat operations.

                    4.     Disassembly and inerting.

                    5.     Post blast investigation.

                    6.     Advanced TTPs for EOD tools and equipment.

                    7.     Advanced electronics.

                    8.     Specialized demolition techniques.

                    9.     EOD robotics employment and usage.

                    10.     UXO operations.

                    11.     Destruction of explosive ordnance.

                    12.     Explosive ordnance exploitation.

                    13.     Explosive ordnance reconnaissance.

                    14.     Homemade explosive (HME) ID and neutralization.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (by), Explosive Ordnance Disposal Technician/Officer Training and
Readiness Manual and reference (ba), Marine Corps EOD Program.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Command and Control Center Specialists 55-3015.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     None.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
